residualRisks: public/app.js keeps `capturing` as its render flag while the reducer owns the command guard. They agree today because the capture handler sets `capturing = serverOwnsCapture` from the same frame the reducer consumes, but a future edit that moves one without the other reintroduces the duplicate-command class. The dual-surface rapid-Stop test is the guard.

The just-ended restoration reads `status === "open"` from the meetings list to learn the live meeting. A server that ever marks two meetings open at once, or stops sending the list during capture, would leave `liveMeetingId` stale or null; the restoration then no-ops rather than restoring the wrong meeting, which is the safe direction but is silent.

`#capture-timer` keeps the just-ended duration after idle while the minibar shows none. Truthful (it is that meeting's length) but the two surfaces read differently at rest; if Todo 18 wants them identical it is a one-line clear in stopCaptureTimer, deliberately not taken here.

The raised bound in tests/server-ws-dispatch.test.ts makes a genuine server hang take up to 30s per await to surface. It still fails rather than passing, and the suite remains the only place the real spawned server is exercised.
The native QA client is headless by construction (no AppKit). Real panel bounds, menu-bar item and focus behavior remain covered by Todo 14's evidence, not re-proven here.
